subject: Acme discovery + bake-off: recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Acme discovery + bake-off: recap & next steps

Hi Jordan / Rebecca \u0014

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and so we can get the bake-off scoped quickly. Let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you called out:
- Production latency spikes when serving instruction-following prompts (esp. multi-turn chat).
- High variability in cost across different models / inference stacks; need predictable unit economics.
- Cache/KS reuse is limited in current infra, leading to higher token spend.
- Concern about fallback behavior and graceful degradation during peak load.

Current stack & constraints:
- Running vLLM on an internal k8s cluster for inference; also evaluating TGI (Triton-based) in a standalone cluster.
- Cloud endpoints (OpenAI) used for prototype flows where latency is acceptable.
- Data residency: EU-sourced data must remain in EU region for some workloads (noted but this pilot will be US-only evaluation).

Success criteria for the bake-off (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 250ms for 256-token responses on the target model class.
- Throughput: sustain N concurrent streams (we discussed 50 concurrent requests with batching) with no more than 20% increase in p95 vs single-stream baseline.
- Quality: pass our acceptance eval suite (we will share test prompts) with <= 5% regression vs current reference model on intent/slot accuracy and hallucination rate.
- Cost: lower token inference cost than our cloud baseline or demonstrably better latency/cost tradeoff for on-prem scenarios.
- Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller model variant or cloud endpoints with no more than 2% error-rate during simulated load spikes.

Requested benchmarks for bake-off (please include all in your results):
- Side-by-side: vLLM, TGI, Redwood runtime (quantized and FP16 where applicable), and our current cloud endpoints (OpenAI/Anthropic if possible).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec throughput at different batch sizes, GPU utilization, e2e cost estimate (USD / 1M tokens), and memory/KV-cache behavior over long sequences.
- Test payloads: mixed distribution of short & long prompts, 30% multi-turn, 70% single-turn (we'll share sample prompts).

Attachments: I attached the bake-off template with the acceptance criteria and the data requirements doc. Please review and confirm what we should run on your side vs what you want us to run.

Next steps / timeline:
- You (Acme) to confirm acceptance tests and sample prompts by EOD Friday (10/03).
- Redwood to provide a test matrix + provisional schedule for the 2-week bake-off by Mon 10/06.
- Kickoff run in our staging environment with telemetry collection; we can also run redwood-managed tests if you prefer.

Action items for Acme: confirm prompts, confirm which external endpoints to include, and any additional acceptance constraints.

I'll follow up with a proposed schedule and the HubSpot and Drive links for artifacts.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
[Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx (xlsx, 58 KB)]
[Attachment: acme-data-requirements.pdf (pdf, 120 KB)]

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@acme.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery + bake-off: recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa \u0014 this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Acceptance criteria: can we tighten p95 to 200ms for the 256-token target if the cost delta vs our cloud baseline is <20%? If not, we can keep 250ms as a softer target.
2) Models to include: please include a quantized Llama2-13B (8-bit) and a Vicuna 33B variant in the side-by-side. Also include your recommended Redwood model for the same family.
3) Data / residency: the initial bake-off can be US-only as you noted. For the production rollout we'll need EU residency \u0014 we'll scope that separately.
4) Timeline: 2-week bake-off makes sense. Can we aim to start 10/13 and finish by 10/27? We need results for leadership review on 10/29.

One more ask: please include a simple cost estimate sheet showing monthly inference cost at our baseline QPS (we'll attach our QPS numbers in the prompt set).

Jordan
Director, ML Engineering | Acme Corp
jordan.mills@acme.com
[Inline: On 9/30/2026 2:03 PM, Marissa Cole wrote:]
> Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@acme.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery + bake-off: recap & next steps

Jordan \u0014 thanks, all noted. We can tighten raw p95 target conditional on cost; I'll include both a strict and relaxed acceptance row in the template so leadership can see the trade-offs.

On the models: we'll include the Llama2-13B 8-bit, Vicuna-33B (as requested), and two Redwood-configured variants (FP16 and 8-bit quantized). We'll also run the cloud endpoints you list (please attach the keys/endpoint names to the shared Drive link or tell us which ones to call).

Proposed schedule (draft):
- 10/06: Redwood shares full test matrix + raw infra requirements (GPU types, container images, sample run commands).
- 10/10: Acme confirms prompts and sample dataset in Drive.
- 10/13: Bake-off kickoff (week 1: baseline & single-stream tests; week 2: concurrency and reliability).
- 10/27: Final report delivered.

I'll also attach our initial performance baseline CSV to give your team an idea of what we'll compare against.

Do you want Redwood to run the managed tests (we can run in our staging with metrics exported) or do you prefer to run in your cluster and share telemetry? Both are fine \u0014 managed runs are faster to start.

Thanks,

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-performance-baseline.csv (csv, 12 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme discovery + bake-off: recap & next steps

Aisha / Dev \u0014 forwarding the thread with Acme. They want a 2-week bake-off starting 10/13, include vLLM and TGI in the side-by-side plus our Redwood runtime (FP16 + 8-bit). Key asks: p95 target ~200-250ms for 256 tokens, throughput profile at 50 concurrent streams, and cost delta vs cloud.

Technical asks for the engineering run (please confirm feasibility and earliest start date):
- Models to run: Llama2-13B 8-bit (vLLM), Vicuna-33B (TGI), Redwood FP16 13B, Redwood 8-bit 13B.
- Test harness: use the attached bake-off template (redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx) for reporting; produce CSV results compatible with our baseline.
- Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec at batch sizes [1,4,8], GPU util, memory footprint, and KV-cache hit/eviction behavior over 10k-step sequences.
- Environment: if we do managed runs, use g5.12xlarge-ish hardware or equivalent (we discussed specific GPU types in meeting notes). If Acme wants to run on-prem, we'll provide a lightweight container and a telemetry collector.
- Comparison points: vLLM (latest stable), TGI (latest), and cloud endpoints (OpenAI text-generation/ chat endpoints). For cloud endpoints include cost-per-1M-tokens projection.

Acceptance criteria reference (from thread):
- p95 <= 200ms (strict) OR p95 <= 250ms with cost <= cloud baseline.
- Quality: <= 5% regression on their eval harness.
- Reliability: failover <2% error during simulated load spikes.

Please reply here with: earliest start date for infra availability, whether you need additional samples or secrets from Acme, and an estimate of the Redwood engineering hours to run the managed execution and analysis. I'll cc Jordan once we have an internal plan.

Thanks \u0014 Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
